prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System (dry fuels, steep terrain, WUI). Baseline: segmentation, time sync, health checks, audit logs; coordination records keep timestamps, participant identities, radio path status. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): primary interface; renders common operating picture (perimeter, projected spread, resources, annotations, role-based symbology); produces Crew Staging Pin (effective time, location accuracy, incident ID); opens/records triage cases; holds jurisdictional constraints before Drone Pilot Operator briefing; marks failed radio route impaired (Orion acknowledges); shows crew acknowledgements. North Lookout Camera Mast: smoke bearing (PTZ/confidence); sends Thermal Spot Snippet. South Lookout Camera Mast: second bearing for triangulation; produces Camera Cleaning Log. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): produces Battery Swap Ticket (to Drone Pilot Operator). Drone Tasking Service: footprints, altitude bands, revisit intervals; no flight-release authority; no launch conflicting with Marigold lanes. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): perimeter, heat/smoke/flame/spot detection; may down-weight Smoke Classifier Module (Ridge Shadow Mask; likelihood, trend, obscuration flag); score not fire declaration. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): terrain-aware wind/humidity/temperature/stability fields; Wind Shift Bulletin; time-indexed weather update flagging changes and products needing recompute. Fire behavior model: spread as probability bands. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger). Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold). East Retardant Loading Pump (Retardant Batch Slip); West Retardant Loading Pump. Crewline Mobile Tablet: Helitack Crew Leader acknowledgements; released context only. Actors: County Emergency Liaison: sends Drone Corridor Permit; receives simplified view. Duty Detection Officer (Orion): triage, accepts observations, recommends escalation. Drone Pilot Operator. Air Attack Supervisor (Redtail): receives aviation map products; deconflicts, verifies ground clear, checks restrictions. Tanker Base Manager: confirms pump readiness. Rules: fireline final only with confidence, sensor age, positional error attributes; map products record source/processing time, model version, acceptance, supersession; conflicts shown, reviewed before promotion. States: Confirmed Ignition; suppression planning begins after Portal promotes accepted location for aviation review; airspace delay blocks dispatch. Airspace Restricted: tasking conditional until Redtail confirms. No autonomous

Document units:
S128: The Air Attack Supervisor reviews the promoted location, the confidence history, and the current airspace status before authorizing reconnaissance or retardant planning.
S129: The Drone Tasking Service converts reconnaissance objectives into trackable missions with launch windows, image requirements, altitude limits, and abort criteria.
S130: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock supports initial attack by keeping assigned aircraft charged, positioned, and ready for rapid launch when mission approval is granted.
S131: Kestrel is required to report launch readiness, aircraft health, and recovery availability before a reconnaissance task can be released.
S132: The Drone Pilot Operator confirms that the proposed route is consistent with field conditions and can be flown without interfering with suppression aircraft.
S133: Reconnaissance imagery is used to verify access, flame spread direction, and exposure to structures before crews are committed to a line assignment.
S134: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine compares recent reconnaissance observations with camera detections and weather-driven projections to support tactical recommendations.
S135: The Smoke Classifier Module remains a supporting source during suppression planning and is not treated as the sole basis for aircraft commitment.
S136: The Air Attack Supervisor uses the Wind Shift Bulletin to reassess aircraft sequencing, holding areas, and drop approach direction.
S137: The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console maintains a planning view of tanker availability, estimated time to target, base turnaround time, and assigned incident priority.
S138: Marigold must prevent a dispatch plan from being released when required aviation approvals, airspace status, or tanker readiness fields are incomplete.
S139: The Airspace Restricted State limits dispatch options until the Air Attack Supervisor confirms that the planned route and working altitude are acceptable.
S140: The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console produces the Runway Release Note after the planned departure sequence has been validated against runway constraints.
S141: The Tanker Base Manager uses the batch slip to confirm that the loading record matches the aircraft assignment and planned retardant quantity.
S142: The East Retardant Loading Pump and West Retardant Loading Pump report equipment state, flow readiness, and out-of-service conditions to support base capacity estimates.
S143: Loading status is displayed as operational information rather than as an approval, so a supervisor decision is still required before aircraft are committed.
S144: The Tanker Base Manager resolves discrepancies in loading status before the dispatch plan is presented as ready for release.
S145: The VHF Radio Gateway Repeater provides an operational fallback for relaying approved aviation instructions when data connectivity is degraded.
